## Goal

Keep the public forms defensible when a dependency is unavailable, and make a newsletter consent record provable later.

## Context

The contact and newsletter forms are the only write surface the first launch opens. Each has two independent protections, and both currently degrade to permissive when their dependency is unreachable. Separately, a local consent record carries the time, wording, version and network data, but for an anonymous submission it carries no reference to the subscriber it belongs to, which weakens a later request to prove or withdraw consent. Details are in the owner's private tracker.

## Scope

- Require at least one working independent protection; when none is available, use a restricted safe mode and make its duration observable.
- Give a consent record an appropriately protected reference to its subscriber, and record the state of the request, its confirmation and any withdrawal, including what the provider reports back.
- A migration if the consent record needs a new field.
- `docs/SECURITY.md` records the degradation rule.

## Out of scope

- Changing the request-origin contract (SC-018).
- Redesigning the forms (SC-005 and later).
- Changing the newsletter provider.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test with both dependencies failing at once shows the restricted mode, not a permissive pass.
- [ ] A test shows a consent record that can be matched to its subscriber and to the provider's confirmation.
- [ ] No plain-text network identifier is stored where the documented masking rule applies.
- [ ] Independent review approves.

## Required tests

- Unit tests for both degradation paths and for the consent record.
- A DB test if a migration lands.
- All standard checks.

## Dependencies

- SC-018
